description: Reference period stored as a date. In gdp_expenditure_quarterly.csv it is the first day of the calendar quarter (1961-01-01 is the first quarter of 1961, 2026-04-01 is the second quarter of 2026). In gdp_by_industry_monthly.csv it is the first day of the month (1997-01-01 to 2026-08-01). In gdp_expenditure_provincial_annual.csv it is January 1 of the calendar year (1981-01-01 to 2025-01-01).

Geography as published. The quarterly and monthly files have Canada only. The annual file has Canada, the ten provinces, Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Northwest Territories including Nunavut (to 1998 only), and Outside Canada.
Statistics Canada Dissemination Geography Unique Identifier for the geography. Empty where none is published, for example Outside Canada.

Price basis as published. Current prices are nominal dollars. Chained (2017) dollars and 2017 constant prices are real (volume) measures. Chained (2017) dollars percentage change is the change from the previous quarter in percent, not annualized. Contributions to percent change show how many percentage points each component added to the change in GDP. Chained (2012) dollars, Chained (2007) dollars and 2012 constant prices are terminated older bases kept as published.

Quarterly and monthly files only. Seasonally adjusted at annual rates means the quarterly or monthly level is shown as if it held for a full year. Unadjusted means raw quarterly values. Trading day adjusted means monthly values adjusted only for the number of working days.

Quarterly and annual files only. Expenditure component as published, for example Household final consumption expenditure, Business gross fixed capital formation, Exports of goods and services, Less: imports of goods and services, Statistical discrepancy, Gross domestic product at market prices and Final domestic demand. Child lines are parts of their parent lines. Imports are shown as positive values and are subtracted to get GDP. Adjusting entry lines in the annual file reconcile chained components with their totals.
Unit of measure for value, as published: Dollars or Percent.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the unit of measure.
Scale of value as published: millions for dollar values and units for percent values. A dollar value of 1000 means 1,000 million dollars, or 1 billion dollars.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the scalar factor.
Statistics Canada vector identifier for the series. Useful if you want to pull the same series again.
Statistics Canada coordinate string that locates the series inside the official table.

The published value. Dollar values are in millions. Percent values are percentages or percentage points. Empty when Statistics Canada did not publish a figure (status ..). Official values were not altered.
Statistics Canada status symbol. .. means not available for that reference period and value is empty. Empty status means a regular published value.
Additional Statistics Canada symbol when present. Empty in all three files in this snapshot.
t if Statistics Canada has terminated this series (older price bases), otherwise empty.
Number of decimal places Statistics Canada uses when displaying the value.
